activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing

Chart: Use a chart with columns for the simple present and present continuous process to show the pupils how - s, -es and ies are added to the verb
Pictures: Show the pupils a series of pictures with sentences underneath narrating what is happening in the images
activities.assessment_criteria: Routines and ongoing activities in school and home contexts are expressed correctly
suggested_resources: Texts and audio/ audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills

Explanation: Compose pairs of simple sentences for pupils to see how and and but are used
activities.assessment_criteria: Conjunctions are used in oral and written contexts

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information

Songs: Use fun songs such as The Wheels on the Bus, Old McDonald, The Itsy Bitsy Spider, Bingo, and Row Row Row Your Boat to learn to pronounce words into syllables
Using pictures: Guide the pupils through identifying and saying multi syllabic words from magazines or online sources
activities.assessment_criteria: Multi-syllable and grade-appropriate words are read correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing
activities.learning_activity: (c) Express possession using adjectives and pronouns (target: my, mine, yours, his, her, hers, their, theirs)
suggested_methods: Songs: Guide the pupils through singing relevant songs with adjectives and pronouns
Games: Use Stop me drills and Hot-chair games to guide the pupils through expressing adjectives and pronouns
activities.assessment_criteria: Possessions are expressed using adjectives and pronouns

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing
activities.learning_activity: (d) Express completed and unfinished actions (structure: present perfect, past perfect tense)
suggested_methods: Dialogue: Prepare a dialogue using present perfect and past perfect tenses and let the pupils practice it
I know What You Will Say Game: Lead the pupils in groups, to complete questions using the present perfect or past simple
activities.assessment_criteria: Completed and unfinished actions are expressed correctly

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing
activities.learning_activity: (e) Use conjunctions in oral and written contexts (target: too… to, either …or, neither…nor)
suggested_methods: Songs: Play a song on conjunction (e.g., “Conjunction Junction” by School House Rock) and guide the pupils through using the song to discuss conjunctions
Describing: Write too… to, either… or and neither… nor on the board and guide the pupils through describing the usage of each of these pairs
Discussion: Guide the pupils through discussing the targeted conjunction and create pairs of simple sentences
activities.assessment_criteria: Conjunctions are used in oral and written contexts

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing
activities.learning_activity: (f) Use active and passive voices to communicate in different contexts
suggested_methods: Active Approach: Guide the pupils through saying the actions after you show the action
Brainstorming: Guide the pupils through brainstorming about things that the government does for the people
Construction: Guide the pupils through using passive voice to report about things done in their communities
Transformation: Guide the pupils through reporting the same events in active voice and later changing them to passive voice
activities.assessment_criteria: Active and passive voices are used appropriately to communicate in different contexts

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Comprehend information presented orally
activities.learning_activity: (a) Follow oral instructions to accomplish a task (e.g., operating equipment and making objects)
suggested_methods: Demonstration: Show the pupils a pre-built structure made from blocks and explain how it was built
Building Blocks: Give a list of clearly written instructions on recreating structures using blocks of their own
Scavenger Hunt Game: Provide the pupils with a set of clues to follow progressively until the treasure is found
activities.assessment_criteria: Oral instructions are followed to accomplish tasks
suggested_resources: Realia, audio/ audiovisual materials, special pencils, stickers, texts with various information

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Comprehend information presented orally
activities.learning_activity: (b) Listen to grade-appropriate myths, fairy tales and fables presented through audio/audiovisual channels and respond accordingly
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the pupils through brainstorming about myths, fairy tales and fables they know
Storytelling: Guide the pupils through narrating myths/fairy tales/fables of their choice to the class
Dramatising: Screen a short fairy tale and tell the pupils in groups to discuss and dramatise it
activities.assessment_criteria: Grade-appropriate myths, fairy tales, and fables are listened to and understood well

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Comprehend information presented orally
activities.learning_activity: (c) Identify major and minor ideas in a story
suggested_methods: Play a Game: Guide the pupils through thinking about facts and the team that comes up with the most facts wins
activities.assessment_criteria: Major and minor ideas are identified from a story

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Comprehend information presented orally
activities.learning_activity: (d) Summarise issues found in the texts heard
suggested_methods: Summarisation: Guide the pupils through identifying and connecting the central idea
activities.assessment_criteria: Issues found in the text heard are summarised

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Comprehend information presented orally
activities.learning_activity: (e) Retell oral texts
suggested_methods: Modelling: Guide the pupils through guided instructions about how to retell a short text
Using pictures/props to retell: Ask the pupils to use printed pictures from the text, puppets, or other related props to retell
Sequence retelling: Guide the pupils through retelling a story
activities.assessment_criteria: Oral texts are retold correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Construct meaning from simple texts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Read grade-appropriate texts to identify their basic components and contents
suggested_methods: Sentence completion: Read phrases to the pupils, stop and give a signal for a pupil to complete a sentence
Discussion: Guide the pupils in manageable groups to read a text and identify its content. Ask them questions after reading
activities.assessment_criteria: Grade-appropriate texts are read properly and their basic components and contents are identified correctly
suggested_resources: Picture, charts, diagrams and simple texts with a variety of issues

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Construct meaning from simple texts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Deduce the general meaning of a text
suggested_methods: Prediction: Allow the pupils to read a paragraph from a selected text, discuss and predict what will happen in the next paragraph
activities.assessment_criteria: General meaning is deduced from a text

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Construct meaning from simple texts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Summarise issues found in the texts read
suggested_methods: Direct explanation: Explain how to summarise issues found in the text
Modelling: Demonstrate how to summarise by “thinking aloud” while reading the text
Using Wh-Questions: Guide the pupils through creating a summary by answering Who, What, When, Where, and Why questions
activities.assessment_criteria: Issues are summarized from the texts read

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.3 Respond appropriately in a familiar communicative context
activities.learning_activity: (a) Identify main points in conversations
suggested_methods: Open-ended questions: Ask the pupils to give details as they express ideas by asking them, ‘Why do you think that happened?’
activities.assessment_criteria: Main points are identified in conversations
suggested_resources: Wall charts, texts and audio/ audiovisual materials with communicative contexts

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.3 Respond appropriately in a familiar communicative context
activities.learning_activity: (b) Respond to compliments, apologies, wishes and sympathy messages
suggested_methods: Explanation: Explain to pupils the meaning of compliments, apologies, wishes and sympathetic messages
Brainstorming: Ask the pupils to identify different things that they praise people for (clothing, hair, job performance, talent, design, hard work)
Roleplay: Guide the pupils through role playing a setting on the board
activities.assessment_criteria: Compliments, apologies, wishes and sympathetic messages are responded to appropriately

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.4 Read appropriately a variety of simple texts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Read aloud grade-level simple texts with the correct rhythm
suggested_methods: Discussion: Lead the pupils in groups to communicate and explore the text before reading
K-W-L: Use the steps to guide the pupils through reading texts
activities.assessment_criteria: Grade-level simple texts are read aloud with the correct rhythm
suggested_resources: Simple texts with a variety of issues

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.4 Read appropriately a variety of simple texts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Reading grade-level prose and poetry with accuracy and appropriate speed
suggested_methods: Ordering: Cut the poem into verses, mix them and ask the pupils to put them in the correct order
Watch Poetry Videos: Play a poem video for the pupils to watch and answer questions after it
Plant a poetree: Instruct the pupils to go outside gather the information and compose a poem
activities.assessment_criteria: Grade-level prose and poetry are read with accuracy and appropriate speed

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in a different context
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate knowledge of the basic features of spoken language
activities.learning_activity: (a) Practise connected speech by linking words(e.g. they’ll, won’t, there’ s)
suggested_methods: Tongue Twisters: Pronounce a tongue twister and ask the pupils to do the same
Catenation or linking: Guide the pupils through attaching a consonant sound at the end of one word e.g “an apple” = “anapple”, “trip over” = “tripover”, “clean up” = “cleanup”
Intrusion: Guide the pupils through inserting a sound between two words often with sounds /i/, /w/ and /r/ e.g , He asked” = “heyasked”, “do it” = “dewit”
Assimilation: Guide the pupils through segmenting words making them behave like another segment that is adjacent to it. Eg., in-pure>impure
Using podcasts: Lead the pupils to listen and practise what they hear from an age-appropriate podcast of a native speaker
activities.assessment_criteria: Words are linked in connected speech
suggested_resources: Wallcharts, texts and audio/ audiovisual materials with features of spoken language

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in a different context
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate knowledge of the basic features of spoken language
activities.learning_activity: (b) Practise connected speech by deleting some sounds (e.g. next door –> nexdoor dad take –> datake most common –> moscommon used to –> useto
suggested_methods: Elision: Guide the pupils through deleting sounds from words orally
activities.assessment_criteria: Utterances are produced in a connected speech by deleting some sounds

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in a different context
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate knowledge of the basic features of spoken language
activities.learning_activity: (c) Use question tags
suggested_methods: How much can you remember game: In groups, the pupils take turns to ask and answer the questions on their cards
activities.assessment_criteria: Question tags are used correctly

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in a different context
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Produce short and basic oral messages with a logical structure and intelligible pronunciation
activities.learning_activity: (a) Make statements about objects and ideas that can be judged as true or false
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Lead the pupils to brainstorm on statements that are true or false
Describing objects: Lead the pupils to describe objects by making statements about them
activities.assessment_criteria: Statements about objects and ideas that can be judged true or false are made
suggested_resources: Realia, word lists, charts, calendars, cards and audio/ audiovisual materials with appropriate vocabulary

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in a different context
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Produce short and basic oral messages with a logical structure and intelligible pronunciation
activities.learning_activity: (b) Present simple speeches about self and family members on familiar topics (e.g. my pet, my brother, birthday party, wedding)
suggested_methods: Modelling or demonstration: Guide the pupils through working in pairs to prepare a speech and present it to the class
Family Photos: Tell the pupils to bring photos of their families and talk about each of the people in the photos
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple speeches about self and family members are presented

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in a different context
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Produce short written messages using appropriate grammar and vocabulary
activities.learning_activity: (a) Identify the form and content of appreciation, thanks and apology notes
suggested_methods: Explanation: Use sentences to distinguish between appreciation, thanks and apology
Dramatising: Provide short scripts with appreciation, thanks and apology content
activities.assessment_criteria: The form and content of appreciation, thanks and apology notes are identified
suggested_resources: Realia, word lists, charts, calendars, cards and audio/ audiovisual materials with appropriate vocabulary

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in a different context
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Produce short written messages using appropriate grammar and vocabulary
activities.learning_activity: (b) Write appreciation, thanks and apology notes to teachers, friends and parents
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the pupils through identifying and writing appreciation or thanks notes on various things
Dialogue: Lead the pupils into pairs to practise dialogues with appreciation, thanks and apology themes
Recite a poem: Provide a poem with five magic words (e.g., please, thank you, excuse me ) for the pupils to recite
activities.assessment_criteria: Appreciation, thanks and apology notes are written to teachers, friends and parents

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in a different context
activities.specific_competence: 3.4 Demonstrate basic skills in creative writing
activities.learning_activity: (a) Create a journal to record inspiring things (at home, at school, from TV and radio programmes, etc.)
suggested_methods: Personalised journal entry: Lead the pupils to write a letter of introduction about themselves
Reflective learning: Dictate sentence stems and let the pupils compare their sentences with their partners
Character writing: Pupils read/listen to a story then use the story ideas to write their own in the journal
Happiness diary : Pupils chat about their happiness (or lack of it) and write about their feelings
Vocabulary stories : Pupils construct a story and write it in their journals before reading it to other pupils
activities.assessment_criteria: A journal is created to record inspiring things
suggested_resources: Picture, charts, diagrams and simple texts with a variety of issues

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in a different context
activities.specific_competence: 3.4 Demonstrate basic skills in creative writing
activities.learning_activity: (b) Devise a topic for a poem from the ideas recorded in a journal
suggested_methods: Gallery Walk: Lead the pupils in groups to read and come up with one-word titles for each poem
activities.assessment_criteria: A topic for a poem is developed from ideas recorded in a journal

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in a different context
activities.specific_competence: 3.4 Demonstrate basic skills in creative writing
activities.learning_activity: (c) Use basic figures of speech (simile, metaphor, personification) to write a four-line stanza
suggested_methods: Explanation: Use similes, metaphors and personification to distinguish these figures of speech in sentences
Paper Bag Poetry Activity: Tell the pupils to pull out a piece of paper from the box and read it out aloud and make their own
Collaborative Poetry: Provide the pupils with strips of paper and ask them to write their best ideas on the strips to make a stanza
activities.assessment_criteria: Basic figures of speech are used correctly to write a four-line stanza

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Develop vocabulary by relating words with objects in the environment
activities.learning_activity: (a) Compose a dialogue using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Use pictures to guide the pupils to brainstorm different objects in different settings
Dialogue: Guide the pupils through reading a dialogue with vocabulary on objects found in different settings
Composing: Guide the pupils through composing dialogues on objects in different settings
Acting: Guide the pupils through ac ting out the composed dialogue
activities.assessment_criteria: Dialogue is composed using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings
suggested_resources: charts and audio/ audiovisual materials with environmental vocabulary

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Develop vocabulary by relating words with objects in the environment
activities.learning_activity: (b) Compose a story using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings
suggested_methods: Finding target a word: Guide the pupils through circling/noting down words referring to objects found in different contexts
Guided composition: Guide the pupils through writing a guided composition
Composing: Guide the pupils through composing a story with specified vocabulary
activities.assessment_criteria: A story is composed using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing
activities.learning_activity: (a) Express nationalities using appropriate adjectives (e.g. Tanzanian, Japanese, Norwegian)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Use pictures of people from different countries to guide the pupils through brainstorming their nationalities
Spot the word: Guide the pupils through identifying the adjectives that describe nationalities in a text and read them aloud
Dialogue: Guide the pupils through preparing and acting out dialogue on nationalities
Role play: Guide the pupils through introducing themselves as members of different nations
Self-introduction: Guide the pupils though introducing themselves by including their nationalities
Role play: Guide the pupils in pairs to a role introducing each other to other people
activities.assessment_criteria: Nationalities are expressed using appropriate adjectives
suggested_resources: texts and audio/ audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing
activities.learning_activity: (b) Use relative pronouns in appropriate contexts (e.g., who, whose, whom)
suggested_methods: Reading: Guide the pupils through reading passages using target relative pronouns
Sentence construction: Guide the pupils through constructing sentences for each of the relative pronouns
Storytelling: Guide the pupils through telling a story using relative pronouns
activities.assessment_criteria: Relative pronouns are used in appropriate contexts

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing
activities.learning_activity: (c) Express future actions (structure: will, shall, going to)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the pupils through brainstorming various actions
Description: Guide the pupils through describing actions presented through pictures orally and in writing
Sentence construction: Guide the pupils to construct oral and written sentences to express future actions/activities
activities.assessment_criteria: Future actions are expressed correctly

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing
activities.learning_activity: (d) Use conjunctions in oral and written contexts (target: yet, despite, in spite of, so… that)
suggested_methods: Finding target grammar: Ask the pupils to circle the target grammar in a passage or dialogue
Sentence re-construction: Guide the pupils through reconstructing different sentences using the circled conjunctions
Sentence construction: Guide the pupils to construct oral/written sentences using the target conjunctions
activities.assessment_criteria: Conjunctions are used in oral and written contexts

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing
activities.learning_activity: (e) Express concession (target: although, though)
suggested_methods: Finding target grammar: Ask the pupils to circle the target grammar in a passage or dialogue
Sentence re-construction: Guide the pupils through constructing different sentences using the circled words
Grammar Challenge: Guide the pupils through constructing sentences with the target grammar
activities.assessment_criteria: Concessions are expressed correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Comprehend information presented orally
activities.learning_activity: (a) Report information heard from a speech
suggested_methods: Presentation: Guide the pupils through listening to an oral speech and report the main ideas orally
Summary: Guide the pupils through summarising information from a speech
activities.assessment_criteria: Information heard from a speech is reported correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Comprehend information presented orally
activities.learning_activity: (b) Participate in dialogues on grade appropriate topical issues
suggested_methods: Dialogue: Guide the pupils through reading a topical issue and acting it out
activities.assessment_criteria: Dialogues are made on grade-appropriate topical issues

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Comprehend information presented orally
activities.learning_activity: (c) Engage in oral discussions on topical issues (e.g. environment, gender, corruption)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Use pictures to guide the pupils through brainstorming vocabulary related to selected topics
Debate: Guide the pupils in teams through conducting debates on selected issues
Chain discussion: Guide the pupils in a circle through discussing given topics
activities.assessment_criteria: Topical issues are discussed orally

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Construct meaning from simple texts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Interpret figurative and idiomatic language from a text (e.g. idioms, riddles, proverbs)
suggested_methods: Finding target words: Guide the pupils through circling riddles, proverbs or idioms in a dialogue or passage
Sentence re-construction: Guide the pupils through creating sentences using the circled words
Questions and answers: Ask the pupils to give the meaning of idiomatic expressions and figurative
activities.assessment_criteria: Figurative and idiomatic language is properly interpreted correctly from a text
suggested_resources: diagrams and simple texts with a variety of issues

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Construct meaning from simple texts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Infer meaning from a text
suggested_methods: Think aloud: Guide the pupils to verbalise their thoughts from the texts they read
Brainstorming: Guide the pupils through brainstorming what they know about the ideas presented in the given texts
activities.assessment_criteria: Meaning is inferred from a text meaningfully

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Construct meaning from simple texts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Relate the content of a text with real life
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the pupils through brainstorming age-appropriate real-life experiences
Reading: Guide the pupils through reading a passage with age-appropriate content
Questions and answers: Guide the pupils through relating the content of the text with real life experience
activities.assessment_criteria: The content of a text is related to real life

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.3 Respond appropriately in a familiar communicative context
activities.learning_activity: (a) Give an appropriate and logical conclusion to a conversation
suggested_methods: Spot the conclusion: Guide the pupils through identifying and reading a conclusion in the text
Dialogue: Guide the pupils through concluding a conversation on a dialogue (e.g., road safety, corruption, gender, e.t.c)
Conversation: Guide the pupils through preparing conversations about environmental pollution and making conclusions
activities.assessment_criteria: The conclusion to conversion is given appropriately and logically
suggested_resources: texts and audio/ audiovisual materials with communicative contexts

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.3 Respond appropriately in a familiar communicative context
activities.learning_activity: (b) Debate on topical issues (e.g. gender, entrepreneurship, corruption, education)
suggested_methods: Debate: Guide the pupils in teams through conducting debates on selected issues
activities.assessment_criteria: Topical issues are debated

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Comprehend oral and written information
activities.specific_competence: 2.3 Respond appropriately in a familiar communicative context
activities.learning_activity: (c) Give appropriate responses to riddles
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the pupils through brainstorming the procedures of playing a riddle game
Riddle list: Ask the pupils to write down all sentences they think are riddles
Riddle game: Guide the pupils in teams through playing a riddle game
Code break: Provide a set of riddles for the pupils to solve within one minute wins a point
activities.assessment_criteria: Appropriate responses are made to riddles

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in different contexts
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate knowledge of the basic features of spoken language
activities.learning_activity: (a) Express feelings using appropriate intonation patterns (e.g., surprise, shock, happiness, sadness)
suggested_methods: Spot it: Guide the pupils through identifying the words that express feelings from a text
Description: Guide the pupils through describing feelings expressed by emojis
Role play: Guide the pupils through role playing and expressing feelings orally
activities.assessment_criteria: Feelings are expressed using appropriate intonation patterns
suggested_resources: diagrams and simple texts with a variety of issues

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in different contexts
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate knowledge of the basic features of spoken language
activities.learning_activity: (b) Use appropriate backchannels in conversations (e.g. so, well, right, uh-huh, wow, yeah, really)
suggested_methods: Dialogue: Guide the pupils through reading a dialogue with appropriate backchannels
Conversation: Guide the pupils through making reservations and bookings
activities.assessment_criteria: Backchannels are used in conversations

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in different contexts
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate knowledge of the basic features of spoken language
activities.learning_activity: (c) Report messages received orally (virtually and face to face)
suggested_methods: Whispering/ Telephone exercise: Whisper a phrase or short sentence to the pupil to pass it on
Announcement: Guide the pupils through making announcements orally
activities.assessment_criteria: Messages received orally are reported correctly

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in different contexts
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Produce short and basic oral messages with a logical structure and intelligible pronunciation
activities.learning_activity: Engage in discussions on a variety of topical issues and defend arguments
suggested_methods: Modelling: Demonstrate how to discuss an issue and defend an argument
Brainstorming: Guide the pupils through thinking, writing and sharing various issues they would like to discuss
Discussion: Guide the pupils through selecting one issue and discussing it
Library search: Guide the pupils through reading the selected topic
Round table: Guide the pupils through stating their ideas topic loudly
Discussion Le ader: Guide the pupils through discussing one pupil’s presentation
activities.assessment_criteria: Discussions and defences are made on a variety of topical issues
suggested_resources: cards and audio/ audiovisual materials with appropriate vocabulary

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in different contexts
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Produce short written messages using appropriate grammar and vocabulary
activities.learning_activity: (a) Develop skills for taking notes from oral presentations
suggested_methods: Modelling: Use audio/audiovisual materials for pupils to see how to take notes
Discussion: Guide the pupils through discussing note-taking skills
activities.assessment_criteria: Skills for taking notes from oral presentations are developed
suggested_resources: cards and audio/ audiovisual materials with appropriate vocabulary

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in different contexts
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Produce short written messages using appropriate grammar and vocabulary
activities.learning_activity: (b) Taking notes from various oral presentations (e.g. speech, lecture, discussion and audio/ audiovisual materials)
suggested_methods: Note taking: Guide the pupils through taking notes from oral speech presentations or audio/ audiovisual materials
activities.assessment_criteria: Notes are taken from various oral presentations

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Communicate effectively in different contexts
activities.specific_competence: 3.4 Demonstrate basic skills in creative writing
activities.learning_activity: Develop a plan for a story (target: setting & plot)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the pupils through brainstorming different settings
Discussion: Guide the pupils through discussing an issue or story they would like to write about
Story map: Guide the pupils through mapping out key parts of the story
activities.assessment_criteria: A plan for a story is developed correctly
suggested_resources: diagrams and simple texts with a variety of issues
